## 操作环境
仅编写和评审具体设计工件，不执行部署、镜像构建、推送或Git历史变更。场景数据为题目给定，示例摘要/域名不能当作可信生产材料。

## 给定材料
checkout应用需要HTTP/WebSocket、数据库、版本关联和可控退出；给定ASGI入口与WSGI可选分支，未提供受支持版本、依赖锁、真实制品或服务验收日志。

## 操作任务
完成协议/生产服务端选择、实际支持参数的启动/输入合同、worker资源/超时/优雅退出/健康/迁移/秘密/版本关联验收矩阵和回退边界。原题只要求解释机制/适用/证据；所有未来测量留未执行，不用启动成功当完整发布。

## 产物
- startup-and-input-contract.yaml
- gunicorn-wsgi-alternative.conf.py
- release-acceptance-matrix.csv
- health-migration-and-secrets.yaml
- engineering-review.md

## engineering-review.md
# Python Web release acceptance applied to the given checkout service
The scenario explicitly includes WebSocket, so choose its actual ASGI entry with a compatible supported server. WSGI is a different callable contract for synchronous HTTP-style applications; the supplied Gunicorn sync configuration is an alternative only if the real application is WSGI and does not require ASGI/WebSocket behavior. Do not interchange imports or use a framework debug server as production acceptance. Existing application/entry changes are developer work, not parameter invention.

The proposed worker/concurrency numbers and 30/40-second drain budgets are hypotheses for this scenario, not measured recommendations. Pin the actual supported Python/server/dependency input set, build in an isolated existing approved environment, run its tests and record an immutable traceable artifact/source digest. No image build, server process or rollout was performed here. Choose existing deployment capability only after separate authorization.

[ASGI specification](https://asgi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/specs/main.html) distinguishes the asynchronous scope/event contract. Python's [WSGI reference documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/wsgiref.html) identifies its reference server as unsuitable for production. [Uvicorn settings](https://uvicorn.dev/settings/) document workers, concurrency and graceful-stop controls; keepalive is not a generic hard request deadline. [Gunicorn settings](https://gunicorn.org/reference/settings/) distinguish worker timeout and graceful timeout; sync-worker behavior must be checked for the installed version. Latest documentation does not pin that version for us.

The acceptance matrix deliberately goes beyond successful startup. Separate liveness, dependency readiness and actual business outcomes; test bounded errors, dependency disconnect/recovery, restart, in-flight HTTP/WebSocket/background work, and memory/CPU/tail latency under representative approved load. Configure only controls the application/proxy/server actually supports. If a hard request/dependency deadline or safe entry interface is absent, stop and request developer support; do not inject logic through a startup command.

Keep configuration/secrets outside the artifact and correlate logs to the actual revision/digest. Apply additive migration and old/new data compatibility gates before rollout/rollback. Missing measurements remain not-executed and cannot be filled from these YAML files. Preserve approved before-state for future recovery, use service/data-owner decisions for irreversible writes, and clean only owned isolated test resources.

# Four distinct delivery contracts
The matrix treats each actual ecosystem separately and distinguishes artifact variants inside it. A library JAR has no obligation to be directly executable; an executable JAR needs the real main-entry and dependency-loader layout; a WAR needs a compatible servlet environment. Never infer java -jar from a .jar or .war suffix alone. [Oracle jar reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/specs/man/jar.html) covers the class/resource archive mechanism; [Maven lifecycle](https://maven.apache.org/guides/introduction/introduction-to-the-lifecycle.html) separates packaging/testing from remote artifact publication.

Python's wheel/sdist flow uses the project's pyproject build backend. A wheel still requires compatible interpreter/platform and any extension ABI; it is not an OS-native self-contained executable. The [PyPA tutorial](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/tutorials/packaging-projects/) separates build frontend, backend and distribution outputs. Do not replace that with historical egg conventions or direct setup.py execution as a universal modern standard. Exact backend and runtime dependencies require separate reviewed resolution inputs.

Frontend JavaScript commonly yields browser assets while a Node service has a runtime entry and dependency/module layout. Node is a runtime, not a Web framework. [Node documentation](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/getting-started/introduction-to-nodejs) and [npm ci](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-ci/) support these distinctions and lock-consistent install behavior; lockfile consistency does not establish lifecycle-script trust or native-addon ABI compatibility. A static asset directory must never contain embedded secrets.

Go usually yields an OS/architecture-specific binary. CGO can introduce C toolchain/libc/dynamic dependency requirements; external certificates/config/assets also remain delivery inputs. [Go cgo documentation](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/cgo) explains C interoperation. Do not say every Go binary is static or portable to all targets; inspect build metadata and actual target dependencies.

This project delivers complete artifact/input/entry/exit and provenance designs for the original explanatory question. It did not execute builds, install dependencies, launch servers or publish artifacts. Missing native toolchain/target evidence remains missing for any future runtime claim. Each ecosystem must eventually supply its own exact command/output/artifact/target evidence; Python tests or static YAML cannot stand in for the other three. Pin supported actual versions from the approved toolchains instead of guessing installed versions from documentation.

## failure-and-recovery.md
# Independent multi-application CD design
Treat checkout, pricing and payments as independently versioned artifacts with explicit consumer/provider contracts. Validate the candidate revision combination with contract tests and appropriate integration checks; green unit tests in each repository do not establish cross-service compatibility. Record actual API/schema/event contracts and artifact/config identities before any separately authorized release. The supplied compatibility table is a design decision matrix, not an execution result.

Introduce additive schema changes that preserve old/new reads and writes, then the provider's backward-compatible API, then the consumer with its new feature disabled. The current payments service remains unchanged when its supported v1 contract is sufficient. Do not force every dependency into one simultaneous deployment transaction. Enable the new pricing path gradually only after the required producer/consumer tests, approved flags and per-cohort business metrics are available. Keep old API/data compatibility through the rollback window; remove old contracts later through a separate reviewed change.

On consumer regression, stop flag progression and return to the verified old path if data semantics remain compatible. If needed, select the consumer's previous approved artifact/config pair; a provider supporting old and new APIs need not be rolled back simultaneously. Before provider rollback, verify no active consumer requires the new API. If new writes cannot be understood by old code, hold code-only rollback and request reviewed forward repair/compensation; do not drop columns or replay payment events. Resolve partial side effects using the actual transaction/event ledger.

Health acceptance includes the effective versions/flags, per-tenant checkout and payment outcomes, errors/latency, dependencies, retries/duplicate prevention and a bounded observation window. Missing telemetry or stale release records stops progression. The explicit schema-contraction/destructive-change gate prohibits removing the old data contract in this release; it does not authorize an irreversible schema cutover. RTO/RPO and actual observed values remain unmeasured until an authorized native environment exists.

This session performs no release, feature-flag change, database migration, shared-service write or image build. The original question asks how to organize the mechanism; these complete applied artifacts preserve its scope without claiming a real multi-service CD run. Future operator commands and raw results must come from the existing supported release systems and authorized exact target. Preserve previous approved tuples and clean only owned rehearsal resources, not shared service or database state.

Keep old API/data compatibility through the rollback window; remove old contracts later through a separate reviewed change.

Before provider rollback, verify no active consumer requires the new API.
